topic: Mastering the Product and Chain Rules in Calculus

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: The Concept of Rates
lecture_lines: The derivative describes an instantaneous rate of change.
Visualize a robot moving along a path.
Speed depends on battery and terrain slope.
animations: Animate a car moving at a steady velocity #FF9900.
Show formula Rate = Change / Time in #00FFFF.

sections.title: The Product Rule: When Factors Multiply
lecture_lines: Product Rule applies to multiplying two functions.
Imagine a rectangle growing in both dimensions.
Area change depends on both width and height.
The rule: derivative is f'g plus fg'.
Total weight gain is the classic example.
animations: Show two functions f(x) and g(x) in #FFCC00.
Animate the expansion of the product f(x)g(x) in #00FF00.

sections.title: The Chain Rule: The 'Matryoshka' Principle
lecture_lines: Chain Rule handles composite, nested functions.
Think of it as the Matryoshka doll principle.
Derive the outer shell, then the inner mechanism.
Multiply rates to find the total change.
A mechanical claw demonstrates this perfectly.
animations: Animate nested boxes for f(g(x)) in #FF66FF.
Show derivative formula using composition in #00FFFF.

sections.title: Synthesis & Complex Application
lecture_lines: Complex functions combine product and chain rules.
Apply rules step-by-step with color coding.
animations: Combine Product and Chain rules on screen #FFFF00.
Highlight final unified derivative steps in #00FF00.

sections.title: Summary & Quick Check
lecture_lines: Multiply two terms? Use the Product Rule.
One function inside another? Use Chain Rule.
Check your understanding with our final quiz.
animations: Review key formulas one by one in #FF9900.
